summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve a revision to the Oregon State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) on December 17, 2025, for the Portland and Salem/Keizer, Oregon 1979 1-hour ozone maintenance areas. The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The proposed revisions also include more widespread adoption of Stage I Enhanced Vapor Recovery, Stage I vapor balance, and enhanced conventional nozzles, among other changes. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.

title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that certain wing skin outer mold line (OML) penetrating fasteners installed using threaded nuts without cap seals do not provide reliable protection against potential ignition sources when subjected to direct attachment lightning currents. This proposed AD would require inspecting between certain ribs on the left and right wing for wing skin penetrating fasteners with a threaded nut adjacent to the electromagnetic effects (EME) sleeve; inspecting the left and right wing fuel tanks, surge tanks, and dry bays for threaded nuts installed on fasteners that penetrate the upper and lower wing skins; accomplishing the inspection specified in a certain airworthiness limitation (AWL); and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also require accomplishing concurrent requirements and revising the maintenance program to incorporate the airworthiness limitation task. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Diamond Aircraft Industries GmbH (DAI) Model DA 50 C airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of flap actuator failures. This proposed AD would require inspecting for displacement of the black slide grommet and inspecting the rod end bearing for a tight fit of the flap actuator. This proposed AD would also require modification of the flap actuator followed by repetitive inspections for a broken actuator torque seal on the jam nuts at the attachment of the rod end bearing of the flap actuator with applicable corrective action. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of unmodified flap actuators on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Dassault Aviation Model MYSTERE-FALCON 50, FALCON 2000, and FALCON 2000EX airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a reported quality escape and a determination that high-temperature oxidation of main landing gear (MLG) upper and lower torque links may have occurred during manufacturing. This proposed AD would require replacing any affected MLG with a serviceable MLG. This proposed AD would also limit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
